clue.text: Firearm that is a wedding security-device

parts.note: a wedding is a match, a marriage between two people
a lock is a device that keeps a door secure

explanation.surface: A gun that turns up as a wedding's security device.
explanation.definitionFit: An early musket fired by a slow-burning cord brought down onto the powder is this kind of gun.

explanation.surface: Asking for a bloom belonging to a warrior woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: something that flows, i.e. a river, here the great South American one.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American river is a flower in the flowing sense; in Greek myth the same name belongs to a race of women warriors.

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we want a word sounding like the synonym for vendor

parts.note: a vendor is a seller, someone who sells goods

explanation.surface: A wine merchant is named in a report about stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is stored underground, so the store of bottles kept below the house is named for that room.

parts.note: a building that cannot stand on its own but rests against a wall of another structure

explanation.surface: A business that cannot pay its own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-supporting' suggests money, but it is literal: this shed props itself against another building.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple shed with a sloping roof propped against an existing wall is not self-supporting.

clue.text: Smoker's aid to get the air colder perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words before it may be shuffled into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A gadget for smokers that might cool the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GET THE AIR COLDER, all fifteen letters; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim tube in which a smoker holds a cigarette is a classic accessory for smoking.

clue.text: Mixed drinks mulled as a weapon

parts.note: a sling is a mixed drink of spirits, sugar and water, as in Singapore sling
mulled wine is heated and spiced, so served hot

explanation.surface: Cocktails and mulled wine as a dangerous combination.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked stick with an elastic band for firing stones is a child's weapon.

clue.text: Young Diana's set off for dilapidation

parts.note: Di is the short, familiar form of Diana, plus the possessive s
to repair to a place is to set off for it, to go there

explanation.surface: A young woman named Diana sets out on a journey to a ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A building in poor condition through neglect has fallen into dilapidation.

clue.text: Evidence of the policy to come?

definitions.text: Evidence of the policy to come?

parts.words: Evidence of the policy to come?
parts.note: a temporary document from an insurer proving protection until the full policy is issued

explanation.surface: Proof of a government plan still to be announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policy' suggests politics but means an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer issues this interim document as proof of insurance before the formal policy arrives.

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words on bail are scrambled into another order

explanation.surface: A dull character released on bail.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or animal lacking pigment in skin and hair is pale, without colour.

parts.note: a measurement taken across the tracks of a railway, from one rail to the other

explanation.surface: Seeing the hidden meaning in a text.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for inferring hidden meaning is read literally: a reading (measurement) between railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The distance between the two rails of a track is measured and given as a standard figure.

clue.text: Part of course said to come in from France

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the French verb is pronounced to give the dish

parts.note: entrer is the French verb meaning to enter, to come in

explanation.surface: Someone arriving from France during a part of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from France' asks for French: entrer, 'to come in', sounds just like the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish served between the fish and the main course, or in the US the main dish itself, is part of a meal.

parts.note: the Black Friars were Dominicans; their home is a religious house, cut off from the world

explanation.surface: A remote house in the Blackfriars district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackfriars is a London district, but the name comes from the black-robed Dominican friars.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a religious order live secluded in a community house of this kind.

parts.note: spoken aloud, ingrate becomes in grate: a tray collecting the remains of a fire in the fireplace

explanation.surface: Someone who gathers ungrateful people, so rumour says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ingrate' is an ungrateful person, but said aloud it is 'in grate', where the fire burns.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray beneath a fire grate collects the cinders and remains of the fire.

clue.text: Last person in tug-of-war team produces a fluke

definitions.text: Last person in tug-of-war team produces a fluke

parts.words: Last person in tug-of-war team produces a fluke
parts.note: the rear puller in a tug-of-war team has a title naming a ship's heavy hook, whose arms are flukes

explanation.surface: The back member of a tug-of-war side wins by a lucky chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluke' looks like a lucky chance but is the pointed arm of a ship's anchor.
explanation.definitionFit: The heaviest member, placed at the rear of a tug-of-war team, holds it steady like a ship's mooring.

parts.note: someone clamorous is noisy and all talk, full of words but no action

explanation.surface: A loud sergeant-major making polite chatter in high society.
explanation.definitionFit: Light, polite chatter at social gatherings is the typical conversation of society.

parts.note: a woman employed at the pictures to lead patrons to their seats with a torch

explanation.surface: The star actress of the film world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a film star, but here she literally leads people to their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A female attendant guiding filmgoers to their seats is the cinema's lady who leads.

indicators.note: weird suggests something strange, telling us to rearrange the three letters

explanation.surface: A strange ancient letter from a runic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old English letter for the th sound, derived from runes, is an ancient alphabetic character.

indicators.note: some means only part of the word Unearthing is taken

explanation.surface: Digging up an appendage in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city but means the head, as in capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ of hearing sticks out from the side of the head, which is the capital in the sense of top.

parts.note: a stretcher is a brick laid lengthwise; a builder's trough on a pole carries bricks

explanation.surface: A call for medics to carry a casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: In bricklaying a stretcher is a brick laid with its long side showing, not a medical litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder's labourer carries bricks in a V-shaped trough on a pole over the shoulder.

parts.note: bits and pieces are coins here, such as threepenny bits and pieces of eight, so this is a coin expert

explanation.surface: Someone who hoards odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits and pieces' sounds like junk, but bits and pieces are coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A student or collector of coins and medals is a coin specialist.

clue.text: Setback for the German or Rus sian?

indicators.note: set back means turned backwards, so the German word is read in reverse

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Asking whether a defeat befell the Germans or the Russians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' looks like a defeat in the war, but it reverses DER, German for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Communist Russians were commonly called Reds, after the colour of the revolutionary flag.

clue.text: Founder of orchestra taking year as astronomer

parts.note: Sir Charles Halle founded the Manchester orchestra that bears his name

explanation.surface: An orchestra's founder takes a year off to study the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The Halle is a famous orchestra in Manchester, England; 'taking' joins the year to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond, the English scientist who predicted the return of the famous comet, was a stargazer.

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A racing tip urging someone to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present at an event is to go to it and be there.

explanation.surface: Someone bundled up in the manner of a camper.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the second reading is 'in tent', where a camper sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Being engrossed or absorbed means wrapped up in something; read as two words it is where a camper sleeps, under canvas.

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: bonded means glued together, stuck
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Plaster that has not quite set firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter of STUCK, giving STUC.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine plaster applied to walls and mouldings is a type of rendering.

clue.text: Musician's loud eating fish and sitting pretty

indicators.note: eating means one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: forte is the musical term for loud
tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: A loud musician eating fish and enjoying comfortable circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sitting pretty is in a lucky and comfortable position.

clue.text: River animal that is a bit of a bounder

parts.note: the otter is a river-dwelling mammal

explanation.surface: A river animal that tends to leap about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like an animal that bounds, but it is an old British word for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bounder and a cad are both old British words for a dishonourable man.

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters of here and dance are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A quality that holds in a medley of dances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' mixes HERE and DANCE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The property of sticking to something or holding fast is a clinging quality.

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters of atolls are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Coral islands designated for bomb tests.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls nuclear tests on Pacific atolls; 'explosion' rearranges ATOLLS.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion or give out shares is to assign them.

clue.text: Established custom to drain it off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or awry, so the letters of to drain it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-standing habit of draining something away.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom handed down through generations is long established practice.
